name: es20-transformations-camera
title: Transformations and camera
summary: A depth-tested 3D scene (cube, ground, posts, pyramid) drawn through model/view/projection matrices with a perspective and an orthographic pane; the near plane cuts the foreground. Every pixel is checked against a CPU rasterizer of the same coordinate chain.
spec: ES 3.0 §2.13 Coordinate Transformations (clip -> NDC), §2.13.1 Controlling the Viewport (NDC -> window, depth range)
ES 3.0 §2.18 Primitive Clipping (clip volume -w <= x,y,z <= w, polygon clipping against near and far planes)
ES 3.0 §2.12.6.1 Loading Uniform Variables In The Default Uniform Block (UniformMatrix*fv, transpose), §6.1.12 (matrices are returned in column-major order)
ES 3.0 §3.6.1 Basic Polygon Rasterization (point sampling at fragment centers)
ES 3.0 §4.1.5 Depth Buffer Test, §4.2.3 Clearing the Buffers (ClearDepthf), §2.1.6.2 (float to normalized fixed-point conversion)
GLSL ES 3.00 §4.1.6 Matrices, §5.10 Vector and Matrix Operations (column-major), §7.1 Vertex Shader Special Variables (gl_Position)

api.glUniformMatrix4fv: model/view/projection uploaded with transpose = GL_FALSE (column-major) and with GL_TRUE (row-major data); both give a picture that agrees with the CPU rasterizer on ~26000 pixels per pane; glGetUniformfv read-back; row-major data declared column-major is a negative control
api.glGetUniformfv: a non-symmetric 4x4 matrix reads back bit-exactly in column-major order after GL_FALSE and GL_TRUE uploads, and transposed after the wrong upload
api.glGetUniformLocation: six active uniforms (u_model, u_view, u_projection, u_light_dir, u_ambient, u_lit) resolved; a wrong location would change the picture
api.glUniform3f: light direction: shaded face colors agree with the CPU shading model within 2/255
api.glUniform1f: ambient term and the per-draw u_lit switch: shaded cube faces and unshaded gizmo/icon colors agree with the CPU
api.glGenBuffers: one buffer holds all meshes; vertex data observed through the rendered pixels
api.glBindBuffer: ARRAY_BUFFER binding captured by the attribute pointers
api.glBufferData: ~1600 interleaved vertices (position, normal, color) observed through the rendered pixels
api.glBindVertexArray: attribute state restored by binding the VAO
api.glEnableVertexAttribArray: three attributes sourced from the buffer
api.glVertexAttribPointer: interleaved stride 36 / offsets 0, 12, 24: positions, normals (through shading) and colors all observed in the image
api.glDrawArrays: each item is one first/count range of the shared buffer; every item is compared with the CPU rasterizer
api.glViewport: two panes with non-zero origins plus two inset viewports; the NDC -> window mapping is verified at ~26000 pixels per pane
api.glScissor: scissored clears stay inside their rectangles: gutter pixels keep the separator color and the second pane does not erase the first
api.glEnable: GL_DEPTH_TEST and GL_SCISSOR_TEST; disabling the depth test changes hidden-surface results exactly as the CPU painter's-order model predicts
api.glDisable: GL_DEPTH_TEST off: the last-drawn face wins (verified against a CPU painter's model); GL_SCISSOR_TEST off before the window clear
api.glIsEnabled: GL_DEPTH_TEST state after the scene, after glDisable and after glEnable
api.glDepthFunc: GL_LESS (nearest wins, hidden faces stay hidden) and GL_GREATER with the depth buffer cleared to 0 (farthest wins, back faces appear), both compared pixel by pixel with the CPU model; the other six functions are covered by es20-depth-test
api.glClearDepthf: 0.0 makes GL_GREATER usable: the whole-pane comparison fails if the clear value were ignored
api.glClearColor: pane, separator and inset clear colors observed in the gutter and background pixels
api.glClear: color+depth clears limited by the scissor rectangle

visual_review.notes: radeonsi es-max and zink es-min captures (256x256) plus 960x540, 1024x512 and 640x640 renders and a keyboard-driven xvfb run: two stacked panes (perspective with a wedge icon on top, orthographic with a box icon below); tumbling cube with green top, blue and red sides, small orbiting cube, ground checkerboard with red X-axis row, blue Z-axis column and white origin tile, pyramid, axis gizmo bottom right. Three identical posts shrink with distance in the perspective pane and keep their height in the orthographic one; the nearest post and the ground are cut off by the near plane (hollow, darker inside; ground ends in a straight line above the bottom edge). Orbit, dolly, elevation and P (projection mode) keys change the view; dollying in cuts the cube open at the near plane.
